title: Java4Shell: OpenJDK Base64 memory corruption (CVE-2026-114938)
summary: Calif disclosed a critical memory-corruption flaw in the optimized Base64 decoder of affected OpenJDK builds. On certain x86-64 processors with AVX-512 VBMI, malformed padded input can trigger an out-of-bounds heap write, and researchers demonstrated pre-authentication remote code execution against several enterprise Java products. Patches were announced November 17. No widespread exploitation has been verified.
fix: Patched OpenJDK builds announced November 17. Runtimes need inventorying and updating; exposure depends on CPU and runtime build.

rootCause.summary: An out-of-bounds heap write in the optimized Base64 decoder intrinsic, reachable with malformed padded input on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI.

history.summary: Calif disclosed CVE-2026-114938 with pre-authentication remote code execution demonstrations against default configurations of Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, Artifactory and PingFederate.
Patches were announced. The demonstrations do not prove that every Java deployment is exploitable, and no widespread exploitation in the wild has been established.
